title: Relation (IV) of Nakamura and Schneps holds on the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group, with an application to the two elliptic points of the modular curve
subject: math.GR
abstract: Nakamura and Schneps (2000) defined a subgroup of the profinite Grothendieck--Teichmüller group $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ by two relations, $(\mathrm{III}')$ and $(\mathrm{IV})$, that hold for Galois elements; they proved that it acts on the profinite mapping class groups of all surfaces, and left open whether it is all of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. We prove that $(\mathrm{IV})$ holds for every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. It follows that every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ is the product of a Galois element and an element of the group $\Lambda$ of Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps, which acts on the whole tower of pure mapping class groups by their formulas. As an application we study a character $\delta$ with values in $\mathbf F_2$, defined on the larger group given by the two- and three-cycle relations alone, which compares at level twelve how an element moves the two elliptic points of the modular curve. We prove that $\delta$ vanishes on the normalized elements of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, so that every character extending it and trivial on Galois elements is trivial on $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. The proofs use the theorem of Boggi and Zalesskii on finite $p$-subgroups of profinite completions, the action of Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps, and the theorem of Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki on the outer automorphisms of genus-zero configuration groups. Relation $(\mathrm{III}')$ is not touched. The mathematics was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode); it was checked by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max, which wrote this text and rewrote several proofs, and by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max as second reader. No human has checked it.
comments:
Relation (IV) is H. Nakamura's; the subgroup it defines with (III') is Nakamura and Schneps's (Invent. Math. 2000), who proved that Galois elements satisfy it and left open whether the subgroup is all of GT-hat; Lochak, Nakamura and Schneps (February 2026) still called this unclear. The group Lambda and its action on the tower are Hatcher, Lochak and Schneps's; the implication from the normalized relation (IV) to their relation (R) is Schneps's. The proofs rest on the theorem of Boggi and Zalesskii on finite p-subgroups of profinite mapping class groups and on the theorem of Hoshi, Minamide and Mochizuki on the outer automorphisms of genus-zero configuration groups. New here: (IV) on all of GT-hat, the decomposition GT-hat = Lambda_0 . G_Q, and the vanishing of the level-twelve character delta on normalized elements.

Checks: Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max checked the proofs, wrote the text and rewrote several proofs; Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max refereed it as second reader and checked Theorems 1-2 again before deposit. No human has checked it. Records: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/mathematics-workbenches/blob/main/works/WB-0007.md

How it was produced. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, produced the mathematics in research runs of November 2026 on notes of Grothendieck's La longue marche a travers la theorie de Galois, prompted by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) at effort max. Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, wrote the present text on 23 November 2026 as editor, rewriting several proofs (the finite-subgroup steps through Boggi-Zalesskii, the shear lemma, the unit lemma, half of one proposition).

How it was checked. Claude Fable 5.2, at effort max, checked every step of the runs' proofs of Theorems 1 and 2 (18 November), re-proved the final computation independently (21 November) and checked the chain behind the hexagonal self-similarity (23 November). Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, checked the parity computation exhaustively over Z/12 with its own program (22 November) and, as second reader (23 November), followed every step of Sections 4 and 8 and of the rewritten proofs, re-derived the matrix and braid identities, opened Hoshi-Minamide-Mochizuki at the source and found no mathematical error. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, read the text again before deposit and recomputed the steps behind Theorems 1 and 2. A remark on a character Delta of the larger group is cited from the runs and marked as not refereed; it is not used in the theorems. arXiv, the web and Hexagon were searched on 23 November 2026. No human has checked the proofs or the text, and nothing is formalized.
